name: Large 3 in Forged Steel Rigging Ring
title: Large 3 in Forged Steel Rigging Ring for Cabling
h1: Large 3 in Forged Steel Rigging Ring
meta: A large 3 in forged steel rigging ring for tree cabling and bracing systems. Where a ring fits in a cable layout, how to choose one, and how to inspect it.
tagline: A heavy forged ring for joining cables in tree support systems.
summary: This large forged steel rigging ring gives you a solid central connection point when a cabling layout calls for several cables to meet. It is a simple piece of hardware, but in a support system it carries real load, so it has to be the right ring for the job.

body.h: Where a ring fits in a cable system
p: Most tree cabling is point to point: one cable between two leads. On multi-stem trees, some arborists use a hub layout where cables from several leads meet at a central ring. The ring lets each cable pull in its own direction while sharing the load across the crown.

A forged ring holds its shape better than a welded or bent ring, which matters when it sits in the tree for years. Size the ring and the cable together so thimbles and terminations seat properly, and follow the cabling hardware maker's ratings for every component in the system. Browse matching parts in cabling and bracing.
Cabling should be designed and installed by a qualified arborist following ANSI A300 support system practice. Keep all hardware in the system rated and compatible, and avoid mixing unknown parts.

Check installed rings on every inspection cycle for wear where cables bear, corrosion, and any sign of distortion. Replace a ring that shows wear or bending rather than trying to judge how much strength is left.

faq.q: What is a forged steel rigging ring used for in cabling?
faq.a: It serves as a central connection point where several support cables meet, as in a hub layout on a multi-stem tree.

faq.q: Can I use this ring for climbing?
faq.a: No. Use only rings sold and rated for life support when climbing. This ring is cabling and rigging hardware.

name: Husqvarna 12 in Pole Saw Bar, 44 DL
title: Husqvarna Pole Saw Bar, 12 in, 44 DL
h1: Husqvarna 12 in Pole Saw Bar, 44 DL
meta: Husqvarna pole saw bar, 12 inch, with 44 drive links for gas powered pole saws. How to confirm fit, which chain to pair it with, and when to replace a bar.
tagline: A 12 in replacement bar for Husqvarna gas pole saws, 44 drive link chain.
summary: This Husqvarna pole saw bar is a 12 inch replacement guide bar for gas powered pole saws that run a 44 drive link chain. When the rails are worn or the tip is tired, a fresh bar brings back straight, efficient cuts overhead.
highlights: Made for Husqvarna gas pole saws
Direct replacement for a worn bar
specs: Husqvarna gas powered pole saws (check your model)

p: Pole saw bars are not universal. Match the mount pattern, gauge and drive link count to your saw before ordering. The fastest check is the numbers stamped on your current bar and the specs in your operator's manual.

Pair this bar with a matching 44 drive link chain. A chain with the wrong pitch or gauge will not seat in the groove or on the sprocket, and running a mismatched setup wears everything out fast. Matching chain is in chainsaw bars and the chain section.

On a pole saw, a bad bar shows up as cuts that wander or a chain that leans in the groove. Dress light rail burrs with a flat file, flip the bar at each chain change so it wears evenly, and keep the oil hole clear.

Replace the bar when the rails are worn uneven, the groove is too shallow to hold the drive links, or the nose is damaged. A new bar costs less than the time lost fighting a crooked cut at the end of a pole.

faq.q: What chain fits a 12 inch Husqvarna pole saw bar?
faq.a: A chain with 44 drive links in the pitch and gauge stamped on the bar. Confirm against your saw's manual before ordering.

faq.q: Will this bar fit a Husqvarna rear-handle saw?
faq.a: It is meant for Husqvarna gas pole saws. Check the mount pattern for any other saw before you buy.

name: Husqvarna Light Bar 3/8 x .063
title: Husqvarna Light Bar 3/8 x .063 Chainsaw Bar
meta: Husqvarna light bar in 3/8 pitch and .063 gauge for pro chainsaws. Why a lighter bar helps on big saws, how to match chain, and what to check for wear.
tagline: A weight-saving 3/8 x .063 bar for Husqvarna pro saws.
summary: The Husqvarna light bar in 3/8 pitch and .063 gauge cuts weight off the front of a big saw without giving up length. It is a good fit for pro saws used on long days of felling and bucking, where every bit of nose weight shows up in your arms.
highlights: Lighter than a standard solid bar
specs: Choose to match your saw and chain

p: A long bar on a 70 cc or bigger saw puts a lot of weight out front. A light bar trims that, so the saw balances closer to your hands. On a day of bucking or felling, that means less fatigue and better control at the end of the cut.
Light bars still need to be matched correctly. Order the length your saw can pull well, and pair it with a 3/8 pitch, .063 gauge chain with the right drive link count. More bars are in chainsaw bars.
Keep the oil holes and groove clean, check the sprocket nose for play, and file off rail burrs. Flip the bar at chain changes so both rails wear evenly.
Light bars can be less forgiving of pinches and pry loads than solid bars, so avoid levering with the bar. Replace it if the rails are uneven, the groove is shallow, or the bar is bent.

faq.q: What gauge chain goes on a 3/8 x .063 bar?
faq.a: A 3/8 pitch chain in .063 gauge, with the drive link count that matches your bar length.

faq.q: Is a light bar worth it?
faq.a: On bigger saws with longer bars, many cutters find the reduced nose weight is worth it for all-day felling and bucking.

name: Husqvarna 3/8 Micro x .050 44 DL Pole Saw Chain
title: Husqvarna Pole Saw Chain, 3/8 Micro .050, 44 DL
h1: Husqvarna 3/8 Micro x .050 44 DL Pole Saw Chain
meta: Husqvarna pole saw chain in 3/8 micro pitch, .050 gauge, 44 drive links for gas pole saws. How to confirm fit, keep it sharp, and know when to replace it.
tagline: A 44 drive link replacement chain for Husqvarna gas pole saws.
summary: This Husqvarna pole saw chain is a 3/8 micro, .050 gauge, 44 drive link loop for gas powered pole saws with a matching 12 in bar. A sharp chain is what makes overhead pruning cuts fast and clean instead of a slow grind at full reach.
highlights: Sized for Husqvarna gas pole saws
Pairs with a 12 in pole saw bar
specs: Husqvarna gas pole saws (check your model)

p: Three numbers decide fit: pitch, gauge and drive link count. This loop is 3/8 micro pitch, .050 gauge and 44 drive links. Confirm all three against your bar or manual, since pole saws from different years can run different chain.
Keep a spare loop on the truck. Swapping a dull chain takes a few minutes, while filing a pole saw chain in the field is slow. See matching options in chainsaw chain.
Use the file size and angles your chain maker recommends, and keep the depth gauges in spec. A pole saw cuts at awkward angles and often contacts bark grit, so it dulls faster than you might expect.
Retire a chain when the cutters are filed back to the wear mark, when you see cracked tie straps, or when it stretches enough to need constant tensioning.

faq.q: How many drive links does this pole saw chain have?
faq.a: It has 44 drive links, the common count for a 12 in pole saw bar of this pitch and gauge.

faq.q: Will it fit an electric or battery pole saw?
faq.a: Only if that saw calls for the same pitch, gauge and drive link count. Check its manual first.

name: Husqvarna 3/8 Micro x .050 Gauge Chainsaw Chain
title: Husqvarna 3/8 Micro .050 Gauge Chainsaw Chain
h1: Husqvarna 3/8 Micro x .050 Gauge Chainsaw Chain
meta: Husqvarna 3/8 micro .050 gauge chainsaw chain for bars that call for this pitch and gauge. How to choose the loop size, sharpen it, and know when to retire it.
tagline: A 3/8 micro, .050 gauge replacement chain sold to fit your bar length.
summary: This Husqvarna 3/8 micro chain in .050 gauge is a replacement loop for saws and bars that call for this combination. Order it by drive link count to match your bar, and keep a sharp spare ready for the day.

p: Pitch and gauge are stamped on most bars, and drive link count is the number of links that ride in the groove. Count them on your old chain or look up your bar. A chain that is one link off will not tension correctly.
If your saw or pole saw runs 3/8 micro pitch at .050, this is the chain family to match. Not sure? Bring the bar numbers and browse chainsaw chain for the matching loop.
File at the angles the chain maker lists, with the right round file size, and lower the depth gauges a little every few sharpenings. Keep the bar oiled and check tension often while the chain is new.
Replace the chain when cutters reach the wear mark, tie straps crack, or the chain keeps stretching. A worn chain chews up the sprocket and bar nose too.

faq.q: How do I know how many drive links I need?
faq.a: Count the drive links on your old chain or check the bar stamping and your manual.

faq.q: Is 3/8 micro the same as standard 3/8?
faq.a: No. Smaller 3/8 chains will not run on a standard 3/8 sprocket and bar setup. Match what your bar specifies.

name: Husqvarna H47 Full Chisel Skip Tooth Chain 3/8 x .050
title: Husqvarna H47 Full Chisel Skip Chain 3/8 x .050
h1: Husqvarna H47 Full Chisel Skip Tooth Chain 3/8 x .050
meta: Husqvarna H47 full chisel skip tooth chain, 3/8 pitch, .050 gauge. Why skip chain suits long bars and big wood, how to file it, and how to match the loop.
tagline: Full chisel skip chain for long bars and big-diameter wood.
summary: The Husqvarna H47 is a 3/8 pitch, .050 gauge skip chain with full chisel cutters with fewer teeth per loop. On long bars in big wood it pulls fast and clears chips well, which keeps the saw from bogging.
highlights: Suited to long bars and big wood

p: Skip chain removes some cutters from a standard sequence. Fewer cutters mean less drag and more room for chips, which helps a saw pull a long bar through large diameter wood. The tradeoff is a slightly rougher cut and a bit more vibration on small wood.
Full chisel cutters cut fast in clean wood but dull quicker in dirty bark. Use it for felling and bucking big logs, not for stump work near the ground. More loops are in chainsaw chain.
File full chisel with the correct round file and keep the top plate angle consistent. Check depth gauges every few sharpenings.
Order the drive link count that matches your bar length, and confirm your bar is 3/8 pitch and .050 gauge. Running a skip chain on a bar and sprocket in good condition gives the best result.

faq.q: What is skip tooth chain good for?
faq.a: Long bars and large-diameter wood, where fewer cutters reduce drag and help clear chips.

faq.q: Should I run skip chain on a small saw?
faq.a: Usually not. On short bars and smaller wood, a standard full-comp chain cuts smoother.

name: Oregon 3/8 Low Pro x .050 Chain for Stihl MS200T
title: Stihl MS200T Chain: Oregon 3/8 Low Pro x .050
h1: Oregon 3/8 Low Pro x .050 Chain for Stihl MS200T
meta: Oregon replacement Stihl MS200T chain in 3/8 low profile, .050 gauge. How to pick the loop for your bar, sharpen it, and run it safely aloft.
tagline: Replacement 3/8 low profile chain for the Stihl MS200T top-handle saw.
summary: This Oregon replacement for Stihl MS200T chain is a 3/8 low profile, .050 gauge loop that fits the classic top-handle climbing saw. A sharp chain is what lets a small saw make clean pruning cuts and quick limb removals aloft.
highlights: Low kickback design for small saws
specs: 44 DL for 12 in bar, 50 DL for 14 in bar

p: The MS200T ran 12 and 14 in bars in 3/8 low profile and .050 gauge. Count the drive links on your old loop or read your bar to choose the right length, typically 44 links on a 12 in bar and 50 on a 14 in.
Many climbers keep two or three sharp loops in the truck so the saw never goes up dull. Browse more loops in chainsaw chain.

Low profile chain uses a smaller file than standard 3/8. Use the size Oregon lists, hold a steady angle, and keep depth gauges in spec. A dull chain makes you push the saw, which is exactly what you do not want aloft.
Top-handle saws are for trained arborists working in the tree, secured with a lanyard and a separate tie-in. Follow ANSI Z133 and the saw manual.

faq.q: What chain does a Stihl MS200T use?
faq.a: 3/8 low profile pitch, .050 gauge, with the drive link count set by your bar length.

faq.q: Is Oregon chain OK on a Stihl saw?
faq.a: Yes, when pitch, gauge and drive links match the bar and sprocket.

name: Basic Chainsaw Lanyard with Snap
title: Basic Chainsaw Lanyard with Snap
meta: A basic chainsaw lanyard with a snap for clipping a saw to your saddle. How a saw lanyard keeps tools from dropping, how to set it up, and what to inspect.
tagline: A simple, reliable saw lanyard for clipping a chainsaw to your saddle.
summary: This basic chainsaw lanyard with a snap keeps your saw tied to your saddle while you climb and cut. It is the simple version: a lanyard, a snap on one end, and nothing extra to snag.
highlights: Works with most saddle tool rings

p: A dropped saw can kill someone on the ground and ruins the saw. A saw lanyard ties the saw to your saddle so you can let go of it to move, reset your lanyard or handle a limb without it falling.

Attach the lanyard to the saw's tie ring and clip the other end to a dedicated tool attachment point on your saddle. Keep the length short enough that the saw does not hang near your legs. See other styles in chainsaw lanyards.
A saw lanyard is a tool tether. Never clip it into your climbing system or use it to hold your weight.
Check the snap gate, spring and the lanyard itself before each climb. Look for cuts, heat damage from the muffler and worn stitching. Replace it if anything looks off.

faq.q: Where should I clip my chainsaw lanyard?
faq.a: To a tool attachment point on your saddle meant for tools, never to your life-support connection points.

faq.q: Can a saw lanyard hold me?
faq.a: No. It is a tool tether only and must never be used as life support.

name: Bungee Chainsaw Lanyard with Carabiner
title: Bungee Chainsaw Lanyard with Carabiner
meta: A bungee chainsaw lanyard with a carabiner that stretches as you cut and pulls slack back in. How it compares to a fixed lanyard and how to inspect it.
tagline: A stretch saw lanyard that stays short when stowed and reaches when you cut.
summary: This bungee chainsaw lanyard with a carabiner stretches when you reach with the saw and pulls back in when you let it hang. That keeps the saw close to your body and the lanyard out of the way while you work aloft.
highlights: Bungee core stretches with your reach
Keeps the saw close when stowed

p: A fixed saw lanyard has a set length: too short and it limits your reach, too long and the saw swings and catches. A bungee lanyard solves both by stretching under use and contracting when the saw hangs.
Many climbers like a bungee lanyard for pruning and removals where they cut at different reaches all day. Compare other styles in chainsaw lanyards.
Clip the carabiner to a tool point on your saddle and the other end to the saw's tie ring. It is a tool tether only, never part of your climbing system.
Bungee loses stretch with age and sun. Check for a cut or stiff sheath, hot muffler damage and a sticky carabiner gate. Replace it when it no longer pulls the saw back in.

faq.q: Why use a bungee saw lanyard?
faq.a: It keeps the saw close when hanging and still lets you reach when cutting, so there is less slack to snag.

faq.q: How long does a bungee lanyard last?
faq.a: It depends on use and sun exposure. Replace it when the bungee loses its pull or the sheath is damaged.

name: Chainsaw Strap with Ring
title: Chainsaw Strap with Ring for Saw Lanyards
meta: A chainsaw strap with a ring that gives your saw a solid point to clip a saw lanyard. Where it goes on the saw, how to fit it, and what to check before a climb.
tagline: A strap and ring that gives a saw a secure lanyard attachment point.
summary: This chainsaw strap with a ring adds a clean attachment point to a saw so you can clip a saw lanyard to it. It is handy on saws without a built-in tie ring, or where you want the lanyard to hang from a better spot.
highlights: Adds a lanyard attachment ring to a saw
Works with snap or carabiner lanyards

p: Most top-handle saws have a tie ring at the rear, but rear-handle saws and some pole saws do not. A strap with a ring gives you a dedicated point to clip a lanyard so the saw can be carried aloft or hoisted safely.
Fit the strap snug around a solid part of the saw, clear of the chain, controls and the muffler. Then clip a saw lanyard to the ring. More options are in chainsaw lanyards.
Pull test the strap with the saw before you leave the ground. It should not slide, twist into the controls or rest against hot parts.
Inspect the strap for cuts and heat damage and the ring for wear. This strap is for tools only and must never be used as part of a climbing system.

faq.q: Do I need a strap if my saw has a tie ring?
faq.a: Not usually. A strap is most useful on saws without a built-in attachment point.

faq.q: Can I hoist a saw with this strap?
faq.a: Yes, as a tool attachment point, as long as it is snug, undamaged and clear of hot parts.

name: Ring and Ring Bungee Chainsaw Lanyard
keyword: ring and ring bungee chainsaw lanyard
title: Ring and Ring Bungee Chainsaw Lanyard
h1: Ring and Ring Bungee Chainsaw Lanyard
meta: A ring and ring bungee chainsaw lanyard with a ring at each end for flexible saw attachment. How climbers set it up, and what to inspect before each climb.
tagline: A stretch saw lanyard with rings at both ends for flexible setups.
summary: This ring and ring bungee chainsaw lanyard has a ring at each end, so you choose how it connects to your saw and saddle. The bungee body stretches when you reach and pulls the saw back in when it hangs.
highlights: Pairs with your own carabiners or snaps

p: Rings let you build the setup you want. Add a snap at the saddle end and a small carabiner at the saw, or girth one ring to a tool loop. You can swap connectors without replacing the whole lanyard.
The bungee keeps the saw close when you let go and gives you reach when you cut. That combination cuts down on snags in tight canopies. Compare other styles in chainsaw lanyards.
Attach the saddle end to a tool point and the saw end to the saw's tie ring or a saw strap. Never connect a saw lanyard to your life-support system.
Check the bungee for lost stretch, cuts or muffler burns, and the rings for wear. Replace the lanyard once it stops pulling the saw back in reliably.

faq.q: What connectors go on a ring and ring lanyard?
faq.a: Usually a snap or small carabiner at each end, chosen to fit your saddle tool point and saw tie ring.

faq.q: Can I use a ring and ring lanyard for positioning?
faq.a: No. A chainsaw lanyard is for the saw only, never for climber positioning or life support.

name: Arbortec BreatheFlex Pro Realtree Camo Chainsaw Pants, Brown
title: Arbortec BreatheFlex Pro Camo Chainsaw Pants, Brown
h1: Arbortec BreatheFlex Pro Realtree Camo Chainsaw Pants, Brown
meta: Arbortec BreatheFlex Pro chainsaw pants in Realtree camo and brown. Light, breathable saw protection for climbers and ground crews, with fit and care notes.
tagline: Lightweight, stretchy chainsaw protective pants in Realtree camo with brown accents.
summary: The Arbortec BreatheFlex Pro chainsaw pants in Realtree camo with brown accents give climbers and ground crews saw protection in a light, breathable, stretch fit. They are built to be worn all day, up the tree and on the ground.
highlights: Built for climbing and ground work
specs: See label and Arbortec product sheet

p: Chaps work well on the ground, but they flap, catch and get hot when you climb. Saw pants put the cut-resistant layers into the trouser itself, so there is nothing loose to snag on a limb or your saddle.
The BreatheFlex Pro is Arbortec's lighter, more breathable line, made for long days and hot weather. This version pairs Realtree camo with brown accents. Compare colors and fits in chainsaw pants.

Check the label for the protection type and class, and make sure it meets what your employer and ANSI Z133 call for on your work. Saw protection only works if it fits, so choose a size that covers you without bunching.
Wash as Arbortec instructs. Any cut that reaches the protective layer means the pants are done and should be replaced, not patched.

faq.q: Are the BreatheFlex Pro pants good for climbing?
faq.a: Yes. They are designed to be light and flexible enough to climb in while still giving saw protection.

faq.q: Can I repair cut chainsaw pants?
faq.a: No. If a cut reaches the protective layer, replace the pants.

name: Husqvarna 585 Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna 585 Chainsaw: Big-Wood Pro Saw Overview
meta: The Husqvarna 585 is a large rear-handle pro chainsaw for felling and bucking big wood. What it is built for, bar choices, and what to check when buying one.
tagline: A big rear-handle Husqvarna saw for felling and bucking large timber.
summary: The Husqvarna 585 is a large-displacement rear-handle chainsaw built for felling and bucking big wood. It sits in the big-saw end of the Husqvarna range, where long bars and large trunks are the everyday job.
highlights: Built for felling and bucking big wood

p: A saw this size earns its keep on removals and storm work with large trunks, felling big spars and bucking heavy wood on the ground. It pulls long bars that smaller saws would struggle with.
It is a ground saw. Climbers working aloft use top-handle or small rear-handle saws, then the big saw finishes the trunk on the ground. Browse other models in chainsaws.
The 585 may be harder to find new than current Husqvarna models, so check parts support and confirm the exact specs, bar mount and recommended bar lengths with Husqvarna or the seller.

Run it with chaps or saw pants, a helmet with face and hearing protection, gloves and saw boots. Keep the chain brake, chain catcher and throttle lockout in working order, and follow ANSI Z133 and the operator's manual.

faq.q: Is the Husqvarna 585 a pro saw?
faq.a: Yes. It is a large rear-handle saw aimed at professional felling and bucking.

faq.q: What bar length should I run on a 585?
faq.a: Use the lengths Husqvarna lists for the saw, chosen for the wood you cut most.

name: Big 8 Aluminum Rescue Descender
title: Big 8 Aluminum Rescue Descender
meta: A big 8 aluminum rescue descender for lowering and rappel on large rope. How a rescue 8 works, where it fits in tree work, and how to inspect it before use.
tagline: A large aluminum figure 8 with ears for controlled descents on big rope.
summary: This big 8 aluminum rescue descender is a large figure 8 style device for controlled descents and lowering. The ears help keep the rope from forming a girth hitch, and the size suits larger rope diameters common in rescue.
highlights: Ears help prevent locking off by accident

p: Rope wraps through the large hole and around the neck, and friction controls the speed of the descent. The ears keep the rope from riding up and forming a girth hitch, and they give you a place to tie off.

In tree work, a rescue 8 shows up in aerial rescue kits and some lowering setups. It is simple and light, but it does not self-brake, so the operator must keep a brake hand on the rope at all times. See other options in ascent and descent.

Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers. Practice aerial rescue with a qualified trainer before you rely on it.
Check for grooves worn by the rope, sharp edges, cracks and any damage from drops. Aluminum wears faster than steel, so retire a device with deep grooves.

faq.q: Does a rescue 8 lock off on its own?
faq.a: No. It needs a constant brake hand. Learn proper tie-off methods from a qualified trainer.

faq.q: Is a rescue 8 good for tree climbing?
faq.a: It is mostly used for rescue and rappel, not for working-positioning climbing systems.

name: Petzl Maestro S Descender
title: Petzl Maestro S Descender with Pulley for Rescue
meta: The Petzl Maestro S is a descender with a built-in pulley for lowering and hauling in rescue and rigging systems. Rope range, uses, and inspection notes.
tagline: A descender with an integrated pulley for lowering and switching to haul.
summary: The Petzl Maestro S is a descender with an integrated pulley built for lowering and hauling in rescue systems. It lets an operator lower a load and switch to a raise without rebuilding the system.
highlights: Lower and raise in one device

p: In a rescue, you often need to lower, then raise a little to clear an edge or release a load. The Maestro S combines a descender with a pulley and cam, so the same device handles both jobs.
For tree crews, it fits aerial rescue and technical lowering systems. It is a specialized tool, best for teams that train on rope rescue. Other devices are in ascent and descent.

The Maestro S is sized for 10.5 to 11.5 mm rope. Check your rope against Petzl's compatibility list, since many arborist climbing lines are larger. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers.
Inspect the cam, pulley sheave, handle and side plate before each use, and follow Petzl's inspection procedure and records.

faq.q: What rope does the Petzl Maestro S take?
faq.a: Petzl lists 10.5 to 11.5 mm rope for the S. Larger rope calls for the Maestro L.

faq.q: Is the Maestro S a climbing device?
faq.a: It is a rescue lowering and hauling device, not a work-positioning climbing tool.

name: Petzl RIG Descender
title: Petzl RIG Self-Braking Descender
meta: The Petzl RIG is a compact self-braking descender for rope access and rescue on 10.5 to 11.5 mm rope. How it works, where it fits in tree work, and care tips.
tagline: A compact self-braking descender for rope access and rescue.
summary: The Petzl RIG is a compact self-braking descender for work positioning and descent on a single rope. Used widely in rope access, it also shows up in tree crew rescue kits and some single-rope setups.
highlights: Can be installed without removing from harness

p: The rope runs around a cam. Squeeze the handle to release and descend, and let go to stop. The hinged side plate lets you load the rope without unclipping the device from your harness.
For tree work, the RIG suits rescue and some SRS descents, but check rope diameter first. Many arborist climbing ropes are larger than its range. Compare devices in ascent and descent.

Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers. Self-braking devices still need a brake hand on the rope.
Inspect the cam, handle, side plate and wear surfaces, and look for grooves worn by rope. Follow Petzl's inspection procedure and keep records.

faq.q: What rope works with the Petzl RIG?
faq.a: Petzl lists 10.5 to 11.5 mm rope. Check the compatibility list for your specific rope.

faq.q: Is the RIG a good SRS device for arborists?
faq.a: It can descend on SRS, but it is built for rope access. Most arborists use devices designed for tree work.

name: SMC Escape 8 Descender
title: SMC Escape 8 Descender for Rescue and Rappel
meta: The SMC Escape 8 is a figure 8 style descender for rappel and rescue. How it works, where it fits in an arborist rescue kit, and how to inspect it before use.
tagline: A figure 8 style descender for controlled rappel and rescue.
summary: The SMC Escape 8 is a figure 8 style descender for controlled rappel and lowering. It is a simple, durable device that fits in a rescue kit or as a backup descent tool.

p: A figure 8 is the most basic friction descender: rope through the large eye, around the neck, and onto your carabiner. Friction depends on your brake hand and rope type, so there is no automatic lock.
Tree crews use 8s mainly for rescue and rappel, not for working positioning. Keep one in the rescue bag and train with it. See other devices in ascent and descent.

Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers. Learn tie-off methods from a qualified trainer.
Check for rope grooves, sharp edges, cracks and drop damage. Retire the descender if wear grooves are deep or any edge is sharp.

faq.q: Does the SMC Escape 8 self-brake?
faq.a: No. A figure 8 needs a constant brake hand on the rope.

faq.q: What rope works with the Escape 8?
faq.a: Check SMC's instructions for the rope diameter range and the friction it gives on your rope.

name: CT Quick Step Foot Ascender
title: CT Quick Step Foot Ascender for SRS
meta: The CT Quick Step foot ascender from Climbing Technology helps you walk up a single rope. How it speeds SRS ascents, setup tips, and inspection notes.
tagline: A foot ascender that makes SRS rope walking faster and easier.
summary: The CT Quick Step foot ascender from Climbing Technology clamps onto the rope at your boot so your legs do more of the work on a single rope ascent. Paired with a hand or chest ascender, it turns a hard climb into a steady walk up the line.
highlights: Pairs with hand or chest ascender

p: Your legs are stronger than your arms. A foot ascender grabs the rope as you step down and slides up as you lift your foot, so every step moves you up the line.
Most climbers use it with a hand ascender and a chest or hip setup. It helps most on tall trees with a long climb to the tie-in point. See related gear in foot ascenders and foot loops.
Choose the side for your dominant foot and adjust the strap so the ascender sits firmly on your boot. Practice low until the rope feeds smoothly.

A foot ascender is an ascent aid, not your life-support connection. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers. Check the cam teeth, spring and strap before every climb.

faq.q: Do I need a foot ascender for SRS?
faq.a: Not strictly, but it makes ascent much faster and less tiring.

faq.q: Can the Quick Step be my only connection to the rope?
faq.a: No. Always keep a proper life-support connection to your climbing system.

name: CT Quick Step Replacement Strap
title: CT Quick Step Replacement Strap for Foot Ascender
meta: A CT Quick Step replacement strap for the Climbing Technology foot ascender. When to swap a worn strap, how to fit it to your boot, and what to inspect before you climb again.
tagline: A replacement foot strap that keeps a Quick Step snug on your boot.
summary: This CT Quick Step replacement strap fits the Climbing Technology Quick Step foot ascender and keeps it seated on your boot. When the original strap is frayed or stretched, a new one restores a solid, secure fit.
highlights: Replacement for the CT Quick Step
Extends the life of the ascender
specs: Holds the ascender on your boot

p: The strap takes a beating from bark, spurs and boot buckles. Once it frays, stretches or the buckle slips, the ascender can shift on your boot and the rope will not feed cleanly.
Replacing the strap is cheaper than a new ascender and keeps it working the way it should. See more parts in foot ascenders and foot loops.
Follow Climbing Technology's instructions to thread the strap, then adjust it so the ascender sits firmly over your boot. Try a few steps on a rope low to the ground.
Inspect the strap and the ascender cam before every climb. If the cam teeth are worn or the spring is weak, replace the ascender too.

faq.q: Does this strap fit other foot ascenders?
faq.a: It is made for the CT Quick Step. Check fit before using it on another model.

faq.q: How often should I replace the strap?
faq.a: When it frays, stretches, or the buckle no longer holds.

name: CT Quick Tree Spur-Mounted Ascender
title: CT Quick Tree Spur-Mounted Ascender
meta: The CT Quick Tree is a spur-mounted ascender that lets a climber step up a rope while wearing spurs. How it works on removals and what to check before using it.
tagline: An ascender that mounts on your spur for rope ascent on removals.
summary: The CT Quick Tree spur-mounted ascender from Climbing Technology lets you use foot power on a rope while wearing climbing spurs. On removals, that means you can ascend a line quickly and still be set up to spur the trunk.

p: Standard foot ascenders fit on a boot, which can clash with spur straps. A spur-mounted ascender sits on the spur itself, so you get both: a quick rope ascent and spurs on for the removal.
Spurs are for removals only, not for pruning live trees. Use this device where spurs are appropriate. Compare foot ascenders in foot ascenders and foot loops.
Mount it following Climbing Technology's instructions and check compatibility with your spur model. Practice the rope ascent low first.

The ascender is an ascent aid only. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers. Check the cam, spring and mounting hardware before every climb.

faq.q: Will the Quick Tree fit my spurs?
faq.a: Check Climbing Technology's compatibility notes for your spur model before buying.

faq.q: Can I use it on a pruning climb?
faq.a: Spurs should not be used for pruning, so this is mainly for removals.

name: Edelrid Talon Tree Cruiser
title: Edelrid Talon Tree Cruiser Ascent Aid
meta: The Edelrid Talon tree cruiser is a foot-worn ascent aid for climbing a rope with less effort. What it does, who it suits, and how to set it up and inspect it.
tagline: A foot-worn ascent aid from Edelrid for faster rope climbing.
summary: The Edelrid Talon tree cruiser is a foot-worn ascent aid built to make rope climbing less tiring. It lets your legs carry more of the work on the way up, which helps on tall trees and repeated climbs.

p: On a single rope, most of the effort is in the ascent. A foot-worn aid like the Talon grips the rope as you step and slides as you lift, turning the climb into a steady walk.
It pairs with a hand ascender and a proper SRS system. Check Edelrid's instructions for the rope diameters and setup it is designed for. Related gear is in foot ascenders and foot loops.
Fit it to your boot as Edelrid describes and practice low before going high.

It is an ascent aid only, not life support. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers. Check the cam, spring and straps before every climb.

faq.q: Is the Edelrid Talon a life-support device?
faq.a: No. It is an ascent aid and must be used alongside a proper life-support connection.

faq.q: What rope does the Talon work with?
faq.a: Check Edelrid's instructions for the rope diameter range.

name: Notch Jet Step Foot Ascender
title: Notch Jet Step Foot Ascender for SRS
meta: The Notch Jet Step foot ascender helps climbers walk up a single rope with less effort. How it speeds up SRS ascents, setup tips, and what to inspect.
tagline: A foot ascender from Notch for faster, easier SRS climbing.
summary: The Notch Jet Step foot ascender clamps onto the rope at your boot so your legs drive the climb on a single rope. With a hand ascender above it, it is one of the simplest ways to speed up an SRS ascent.

p: Every step you take with a foot ascender moves you up the rope. Your arms only need to slide the hand ascender up, so you reach the tie-in point with energy left to work.
It shines on tall trees and on days with several climbs. Compare other options in foot ascenders and foot loops.
Adjust the strap so the ascender sits firmly on your boot and the rope feeds smoothly. Practice close to the ground.

It is an ascent aid only. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers. Check the cam teeth, spring and strap before each climb.

faq.q: Which foot do I put the Jet Step on?
faq.a: Most climbers use it on their dominant foot. Check Notch's instructions for left or right versions.

faq.q: Can I descend with the Jet Step on?
faq.a: Remove or disengage it before you descend, as the cam will grip the rope.

name: Petzl Knee Ascent System
title: Petzl Knee Ascent System for Rope Climbing
meta: The Petzl Knee Ascent system links a foot ascender to your harness with a bungee at the knee for faster rope climbing. How it works and how to set it up.
tagline: A bungee knee system that speeds up rope walking with a foot ascender.
summary: The Petzl Knee Ascent system connects your foot ascender to your harness with a bungee that runs up past the knee. It keeps the ascender pulling upward so your stride stays smooth, which makes rope walking faster and less tiring.
highlights: Bungee keeps tension at the knee

p: A foot ascender on its own can lag behind your stride. The Knee Ascent system clips the ascender to your harness through an elastic cord at the knee, so it lifts with your leg on every step.
Paired with a foot ascender and a chest or hand ascender, it creates a rope-walking setup for long SRS ascents. See related gear in foot ascenders and foot loops.
Adjust the length so the bungee keeps light tension without pulling your leg out of line. Follow Petzl's setup steps exactly and test low.

It is an ascent aid only. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers. Inspect the bungee, webbing and connectors before every climb.

faq.q: Does the Knee Ascent system replace a foot ascender?
faq.a: No. It works with a foot ascender to keep it moving with your leg.

faq.q: Which Petzl foot ascenders work with it?
faq.a: Check Petzl's compatibility notes for the version you buy.

name: Reecoil Foot Loop
title: Reecoil Foot Loop for SRS Ascent
meta: A Reecoil foot loop for stepping up a single rope with a hand ascender. How a foot loop helps SRS climbers, how to size it, and what to inspect before a climb.
tagline: A foot loop that pairs with a hand ascender for rope ascent.
summary: The Reecoil foot loop gives you a step to stand in when ascending a rope with a hand ascender. It is a simple way to add leg power to an SRS climb without a full mechanical foot setup.
specs: Rope ascent with a hand ascender

p: Clip the foot loop to your hand ascender, step into it, and stand up. Then slide your hitch or chest device up and repeat. Your legs do the heavy lifting instead of your arms.
Foot loops are light and quick to deploy, which makes them handy for occasional SRS climbs or as a backup. Compare other options in foot ascenders and foot loops.
Adjust the length so you can stand comfortably with the hand ascender at about face height. Practice the rhythm low to the ground.

A foot loop is an ascent aid, not your life-support connection. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers. Check the webbing and stitching for wear before each climb.

faq.q: How long should a foot loop be?
faq.a: Long enough that you stand comfortably with the hand ascender around face height.

faq.q: Can I use a foot loop with a foot ascender?
faq.a: Yes. Some climbers use both for a faster rope-walking setup.

name: CT Quick Arbor Double Hand Ascender
title: CT Quick Arbor Double Hand Ascender
h1: CT Quick Arbor Double Hand Ascender
meta: The CT Quick Arbor is a double-handled ascender from Climbing Technology for SRS tree climbing. How the two-handle grip helps on ascents, plus setup and care.
tagline: A two-handle ascender built for arborist SRS climbing.
summary: The CT Quick Arbor double hand ascender from Climbing Technology gives you two handles on one rope clamp, so you can push with both hands on an SRS ascent. Climbers who spend a lot of time ascending often find the two-handle grip less tiring.

p: A standard hand ascender has one grip. The Quick Arbor adds a second handle so both hands can drive the device up the rope, spreading the effort and helping you keep a steady rhythm.
It pairs well with a foot ascender for a full rope-walking system. Compare other handled ascenders in ascent and descent.
Follow Climbing Technology's instructions for rope diameter and connection points, and test on the ground first.

An ascender is not a descent device. Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers. Inspect the cam teeth, spring, safety catch and frame before every climb.

faq.q: Is the Quick Arbor better than a single-handle ascender?
faq.a: Some climbers prefer the two-handle grip for long ascents. It comes down to your system and feel.

faq.q: Can I descend with the Quick Arbor?
faq.a: No. Switch to a descent device before coming down.

name: ISC Ultrasafe Hand Ascender with Safety Pin
title: ISC Ultrasafe Hand Ascender with Safety Pin
h1: ISC Ultrasafe Hand Ascender with Safety Pin
meta: The ISC Ultrasafe hand ascender with a safety pin helps prevent accidental rope release on SRS ascents. How it works, setup notes and inspection tips.
tagline: A hand ascender with a safety pin to help prevent accidental rope release.
summary: The ISC Ultrasafe hand ascender adds a safety pin that helps stop the cam from opening by accident during an ascent. It is a solid choice for climbers who want an extra level of security on their SRS ascent system.
highlights: Safety pin helps prevent accidental opening

p: On a busy climb, the rope can push against a cam or a branch can knock it. The safety pin on the Ultrasafe helps keep the rope captured until you choose to release it.
It pairs with a foot ascender and your SRS device for a fast ascent. Compare other handled ascenders in ascent and descent.
Check ISC's instructions for rope diameter and the correct connection points. Practice loading and unloading the rope with the pin on the ground.

Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers. Inspect the cam teeth, spring, pin and frame before every climb.

faq.q: What does the safety pin on the Ultrasafe do?
faq.a: It helps prevent the cam from opening and releasing the rope by accident.

faq.q: Can I use this ascender as my only connection?
faq.a: No. Use it as part of a full climbing system with a proper life-support connection.

name: Kong Futura Hand Ascender
title: Kong Futura Hand Ascender for SRS Climbing
meta: The Kong Futura hand ascender is a handled rope clamp for SRS ascents and hauling. How climbers use it, setup and inspection tips, and where it fits.
tagline: A handled rope clamp from Kong for ascent and hauling.
summary: The Kong Futura hand ascender is a handled rope clamp for SRS ascents, and it also gets used for hauling and progress capture. Its ergonomic grip makes it comfortable for long climbs.

p: Slide the Futura up the rope and stand on a foot loop or foot ascender clipped below it. On a rope-walking system, it rides above the chest or hip device as the upper handled clamp.
Outside of climbing, crews use handled ascenders to grab a line for hauling or for progress capture in a simple pull system. See other ascenders in ascent and descent.
Check Kong's instructions for compatible rope diameters and connection points. Practice on the ground first.

Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers. Inspect the cam teeth, spring, safety catch and frame before every use.

faq.q: Is the Kong Futura a left or right hand ascender?
faq.a: Kong offers both versions. Choose the one that fits your dominant hand.

faq.q: Can I use the Futura for hauling?
faq.a: Yes, as a rope grab in a simple haul system, within Kong's instructions.

name: Rock Exotica Unicender
title: Rock Exotica Unicender Mechanical Hitch for MRS
meta: The Rock Exotica Unicender is a mechanical friction device for MRS and SRS tree climbing. How it replaces a hitch, setup tips, and inspection advice.
tagline: A mechanical friction device that replaces a hitch on MRS and SRS.
summary: The Rock Exotica Unicender is a mechanical friction device that takes the place of a friction hitch for MRS climbing and can also be set up for SRS. It tends itself as you climb and holds when you let go.
highlights: Works in MRS and can be set up for SRS

p: A friction hitch works, but it needs tying, dressing and frequent cord replacement. The Unicender gives consistent friction from a machined device, tends easily and does not glaze like a hitch cord.
Climbers who want one device across both MRS and SRS often look at the Unicender. Compare devices in devices for MRS.
Use the rope diameters and setup Rock Exotica lists, and practice low first. Friction varies by rope, so test your rope with the device before climbing high.

Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers. Check the cams, springs, wear surfaces and connection points before each climb.

faq.q: Can the Unicender be used for SRS?
faq.a: Yes, with the setup described in Rock Exotica's instructions.

faq.q: What rope works with the Unicender?
faq.a: Check Rock Exotica's compatibility list for your rope diameter and type.

name: Petzl Chicane Auxiliary Brake
title: Petzl Chicane Auxiliary Brake for SRS
meta: The Petzl Chicane is an auxiliary brake that adds friction to a Zigzag for SRS tree climbing. How it works, setup notes, and inspection tips for arborists.
tagline: An auxiliary brake that turns a Zigzag into an SRS device.
summary: The Petzl Chicane is an auxiliary brake that adds friction to a Petzl Zigzag so it can be used on a single rope. With the Chicane, the Zigzag becomes a smooth SRS work-positioning device.

p: A Zigzag is built for MRS, where the doubled rope supplies extra friction. On a single rope, it needs more. The Chicane sits below the Zigzag and adds that friction so descents stay controlled.
Climbers who already own a Zigzag can add SRS without buying a whole new device. Compare devices in devices for SRS.
Follow Petzl's setup steps exactly and use the rope diameters they list. Test the system low first.

Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers. Inspect the Chicane and Zigzag for wear grooves, damaged parts and smooth action before every climb.

faq.q: Do I need a Chicane to use a Zigzag on SRS?
faq.a: Yes. Petzl specifies the Chicane for SRS use with the Zigzag.

faq.q: Does the Chicane work with other devices?
faq.a: It is designed for the Petzl Zigzag. Check Petzl's instructions.
